justification: GATE-3: the DCP max_site_coverage cap was silently dropped because _get_dcp_value always returned value_min, but the cap (e.g. 65 percent) is stored in value_max. site_coverage_pct came back None, so the engine left the footprint uncapped (~80 percent on Haberfield) and the binding-constraint chain omitted the cap. Read the cap with a prefer_max mode so it flows in and erodes the footprint.

pre_impl.existing_data: DCPControl carries both value_min and value_max; the engine already builds and stores max_site_coverage with its cap in value_max (verified earlier: dcp_setback_controls value_max=65). The site-coverage step then compares the cap against buildable_footprint and erodes it — but only if it reads a non-None percentage.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: _get_dcp_value's docstring said it returns value_min (the minimum requirement), which is correct for setbacks/landscaping but wrong for a CAP control like max_site_coverage whose limit lives in value_max. So the cap silently read as None.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new data source: _get_dcp_value gains a prefer_max flag (value_max with value_min fallback); only the single max_site_coverage call uses it. Setbacks, landscaping and deep-soil keep reading value_min unchanged.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A - pure function change; both helpers operate on DCPControl objects already fetched. No new external call, so upstream Portal/DB failures are unaffected.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - backend computation only; ConstraintArithmeticResult.site_coverage_cap_m2 (float) is unchanged in type, just now populated when a cap exists. The capacity card stays unexposed.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If a council stores its site-coverage cap in value_min instead of value_max, prefer_max falls back to value_min, so the cap is still read; the only remaining gap is a control with neither value populated, which yields no cap (a data-coverage gap, not a silent over-read).

functions.name: _get_dcp_value
functions.input: the DCP controls list, the control type, the dev_type, and an optional prefer_max flag
functions.output: the matched control's value_min by default, or value_max (cap) with a value_min fallback when prefer_max is set
functions.if_none: no matching control returns None; with prefer_max a control missing value_max falls back to its value_min

values: N/A - no regulatory values hardcoded; the percentage cap comes from the matched DCPControl.value_max already extracted from council DCP data.
queries: N/A - no database queries; the function selects from the in-memory DCPControl list already fetched by the brief.

break_it.scenario: A council site-coverage cap is stored in value_max and the lot would otherwise build out to roughly 80 percent
break_it.what_happens: Pre-GATE-3 the cap read as None, so the footprint stayed uncapped and the binding-constraint chain omitted site coverage entirely
break_it.repro: compute_constraint_arithmetic with a max_site_coverage DCPControl(value_max=50) and lot_dimensions provided
break_it.how: the cap is read via prefer_max and applied; test_site_coverage_cap_from_value_max_is_applied asserts site_coverage_cap_m2 == 300 for a 600 m2 lot

break_it.scenario: A council instead records the site-coverage cap in value_min rather than value_max
break_it.what_happens: A strict value_max-only read would miss the cap and again leave the footprint uncapped
break_it.how: prefer_max falls back to value_min when value_max is absent; test_prefer_max_falls_back_to_value_min asserts 50.0

break_it.scenario: Setback and landscaping controls must keep reading the minimum requirement, not the cap
break_it.what_happens: If the prefer_max change leaked to setbacks, the engine would read the wrong value for a minimum control
break_it.how: prefer_max defaults to False so the value_min path is unchanged; test_default_min_path_unchanged_for_setbacks asserts 6.0

break_it.scenario: A development with no site-coverage control at all is assessed by the engine
break_it.what_happens: A missing control could raise or be mis-read as a zero cap that wrongly erodes the footprint
break_it.repro: compute_constraint_arithmetic with dcp_controls that contain no max_site_coverage entry
break_it.how: _get_dcp_value returns None when no control matches and the site-coverage step is skipped; existing no-DCP tests stay green

break_it.scenario: The cap is read correctly but is larger than the buildable footprint already computed
break_it.what_happens: Applying a non-binding cap would erode the footprint below the real setback-limited area
break_it.repro: a 65 percent cap on a lot whose setbacks already limit coverage below 65 percent
break_it.how: the step only erodes when coverage_cap < buildable_footprint (existing guard, unchanged); the cap is recorded but does not over-reduce

post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run the Haberfield brief and confirm the DCP site-coverage cap appears in the computation chain and the footprint is no longer ~80 percent uncapped. GATE-1 part 2 (zone-derived dev_type) and the computation-chain reconciliation remain. Engine stays unexposed (#513 unmerged) until the legality gates complete.
